TB-DAL.note: Thursday night in Arlington: 2-2 Dallas, fresh off a 34-30 comeback at Houston, is an 8.5 to 10 point favorite over 0-4 Tampa Bay and undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who makes his first road start with Baker Mayfield still out.
preview: CeeDee Lamb against a thinned Bucs secondary is the matchup. Lamb leads the NFL with 37 catches and 498 yards after 17 for 189 in Houston; Antoine Winfield Jr. is out 2 to 4 weeks with a rib fracture, so Ifeatu Melifonwu is likely to start at safety, per Bowles, who ruled out Benjamin Morrison (quad) on Wednesday, per SI and Bucs Report.

The teams arrive going opposite ways. Dallas rallied from 16-6 down at halftime to win 34-30 in Houston; Tampa Bay lost 17-14 to Green Bay to fall to 0-4 for the first time since 2013, per the Bucs' site and the Dallas Morning News, its fourth loss by 7 or fewer this year.

Turnovers decide it. Tampa Bay is minus 1.3 a game in turnover margin, tied 27th, and Jalon Daniels' two first half interceptions Sunday led to 10 Green Bay points, per AP and the Bucs' site; the Dallas defense has yet to intercept a pass, per the Bucs' site, and gets an interception or pass defended on 7.9 percent of dropbacks, 32nd in the tracker.

The panel picks Dallas; the split is the margin. Pete Prisco has the Cowboys 34-14 and ESPN's FPI makes them 11.4 point favorites at 87 percent; Covers' Jason Logan leans to the Bucs with the points and SI takes the Over 47.5. The line opened at 9.5, per Covers, and sits between 8.5 and 10 across books Wednesday, with Dallas about -455 on the moneyline.

PHI-JAX.note: Jacksonville (3-1) is a 6.5 to 7 point favorite at Tottenham in the first of its two straight London home games, against a 2-2 Philadelphia team that lost Lane Johnson to retirement Tuesday, traded left guard Cam Jurgens to Baltimore Wednesday and has Saquon Barkley week to week, leaving Will Shipley and the newly promoted Dameon Pierce as the only healthy backs.
preview: The Eagles' patched line against the Jaguars' front is the matchup. Lane Johnson retired Tuesday, so rookie Markel Bell starts again at right tackle, and Cam Jurgens, in the concussion protocol since Monday, was traded to Baltimore Wednesday, per the Inquirer and Pro Football Rumors, leaving Willie Lampkin in line for his first NFL start at left guard, per Bleeding Green Nation and CBS Philadelphia; Jacksonville has 2.5 sacks a game, tied 8th, and Philadelphia allows 3, tied 25th.

The teams are heading in opposite directions. Jacksonville has won 3 of 4, including 22-17 at Cincinnati for Trevor Lawrence's first career win over the Bengals; Philadelphia has lost two straight, 27-7 at Chicago and 24-20 to the Rams after leading 20-10 in the fourth quarter. The Eagles land Saturday morning, less than 36 hours before kickoff, per the Inquirer and PFT.

Third down and the red zone decide it. Jacksonville converts 51.1 percent on third down, 3rd, and scores touchdowns on 81.8 percent of red zone trips, 2nd, the two numbers CBS's Tyler Sullivan leads with; Philadelphia went 0 for 12 on third down against the Rams, per Yahoo and NBC Sports Philadelphia, and is at 35.9 percent for the season, 19th.

The panel is unanimous on Jacksonville and split on the total. Pete Prisco (28-16) and Tyler Sullivan (30-17, Jaguars -6.5) of CBS, SI and Covers (both Jaguars -4.5 early in the week) and Bleacher Report all take the Jaguars, and ESPN's FPI gives them about 73 percent; none of them picks Philadelphia. On the total, both CBS scores land over 42.5, while Covers and PredictEm took the Under at 43.5. The line has moved from 4.5 to 6.5 or 7, with Jacksonville about -355 on the moneyline, and the total from 43.5 to 42.5.

CHI-GB.note: NFC North at Lambeau: 3-1 Chicago, 2-0 with backups since Caleb Williams hurt his hamstring, is a 3 point road favorite with Tyson Bagent starting again, against a 2-2 Green Bay that won 17-14 at Tampa but lost Edgerrin Cooper for the season there.
preview: Chicago's run game against a Packers front without Edgerrin Cooper is the matchup. The Bears' line ranks 2nd and their backs average 4.9 yards a carry, 4th; Green Bay is 23rd in rush EPA allowed and lost Edgerrin Cooper to a torn Achilles at Tampa, placed on injured reserve Tuesday, per Packers.com and Ian Rapoport, while Micah Parsons will not practice this week, per Matt LaFleur.

Both won last week; Chicago did it more convincingly. The Bears beat the Jets 23-12 and held them to 32 offensive plays, a Jets franchise low, and 0 for 7 on third down, per Yahoo, NBC and SNY; the Packers won 17-14 at Tampa on two Jordan Love touchdown passes after surviving two fourth quarter turnovers, per FOX11 and Yahoo.

Third down and the red zone decide it. Chicago converts 47.4 percent on third down, 6th, but scores touchdowns on only 42.1 percent of red zone trips, 30th; Green Bay is last on third down at 26.1 percent and 27th in the red zone at 46.7 percent, so the team that finishes drives wins a game the 3 point spread calls close.

The market and the panel split. Chicago is a 3 point road favorite with a 45.5 total in both ESPN's line and the consensus line, about -148 on the moneyline, and the site's power ratings have the Bears 9th and the Packers 18th; CBS's Pete Prisco takes Green Bay in an upset, the only panel pick reached this week.

HOU-TEN.note: Two 0-4 AFC South teams meet in Nashville and one leaves with its first win: Houston, 16th in the power ratings after a 34-30 loss to Dallas, is a 6.5 to 7.5 point favorite at 32nd ranked Tennessee, which lost 24-18 at Baltimore, with a 38.5 total that is the lowest of Week 5.
preview: Houston's pass rush against Cam Ward is the matchup. The Texans get 3.5 sacks a game, tied 3rd, and pressure on 27.5 percent of dropbacks, 6th in the tracker, behind Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter; Ward ranks 32nd at minus 0.16 EPA per dropback, though his line allows only 1.5 sacks a game, tied 5th.

Both arrive off one score losses. Houston led Dallas 16-6 at halftime and lost 34-30 on CeeDee Lamb's 12 yard touchdown with 40 seconds left; Tennessee covered as an 11.5 point underdog in a 24-18 loss at Baltimore, and Robert Saleh called it Cam Ward's best game this year.

Nico Collins is the swing factor. Houston scored 31 and 30 in his two games and 6 and 17 in the two he missed; he caught 7 passes for 118 yards and 2 touchdowns in Sunday's return from a hamstring, against a Tennessee secondary 30th in the tracker that allows 0.20 EPA per dropback, 29th.

The market and all three site models take Houston. No expert picks could be reached for this card; nflverse has Houston by 7.5 at minus 355, about 75 percent with the margin out, ESPN's feed went from 7 to 6.5 by Tuesday, and the ELO Model (71.5 percent), the Joker (68.4) and the Broly Model (77.5) all pick Houston.

CIN-MIA.note: Cincinnati (2-2), off two straight losses, is a 7 point road favorite at winless Miami (0-4), with Ja'Marr Chase in concussion protocol and Tee Higgins day to day as of Monday and a Dolphins offense that has not scored more than 13 points in a game.
preview: Cincinnati's passing game against Miami's secondary is the matchup. The Dolphins' defensive backs rank 31st in the site's units, allowing 0.22 EPA a dropback, 30th, and Reese Taylor (quad) was ruled out Monday, per the Miami Herald and ESPN's injury feed; how much it matters turns on Ja'Marr Chase (concussion protocol) and Tee Higgins (adductor), neither ruled out by Zac Taylor as of Monday.

Neither side brings momentum. Cincinnati lost 30-27 at Pittsburgh and 22-17 at home to Jacksonville, stopped a yard short with 50 seconds left, per AP and Sharp Football; Miami lost 15-10 at Minnesota running 37 plays to the Vikings' 78, per Yahoo and the Dolphins' site, though Jeff Hafley says the team is "starting to believe."

The pass rush gap is the winning factor. Cincinnati gets 3.5 sacks a game, tied for 3rd, against a Miami line allowing an 8.5 percent sack rate, 26th; Miami gets 1.0 a game, tied for 28th, against a Cincinnati line allowing 5.4 percent, 9th.

No panel picks were reached, but the market and all three site models take Cincinnati. The Bengals are 7 point favorites with a 42.5 total on ESPN's feed and at minus 355 on the money line on nflverse, about 75 percent with the margin out; the ELO Model (66.3 percent), the Joker (77.2) and the Broly Model (77.0) all pick Cincinnati, and the power ratings have it 15th to Miami's 30th. Wednesday afternoon's report on Chase and Higgins is what can move it.

LV-NE.note: 3-1 Las Vegas, off its first loss, 30-27 to Kansas City, visits 2-2 New England, off a 29-26 upset in Buffalo; the Patriots are 3.5 point favorites with a 45.5 total, and Drake Maye's league high 7 interceptions meet a defense built on takeaways, though it forced none against Kansas City.
preview: Drake Maye against the Raiders' takeaways is the matchup. Maye has 7 interceptions, the most in the league, per nflverse; Las Vegas forced 9 turnovers in its first three games, the league high entering Week 4, per the Review-Journal, but none against Kansas City, per nflverse, and is plus 0.8 a game in turnover margin, tied 4th, while New England is minus 1.3, tied 27th.

Both come off one score games with unbeaten teams. New England handed Buffalo its first loss, 29-26, on Efton Chism III's 23 yard touchdown with 1:55 left, and NFL.com moved the Patriots up 3 spots to 9th; Las Vegas took its first loss, 30-27 to unbeaten Kansas City, but covered as a 4.5 point underdog.

The Raiders' rush against a patched line decides it. Las Vegas gets 3.0 sacks a game, tied 5th, and its front ranks 4th in the tracker with pressure on 28.1 percent of dropbacks, 5th; New England allows 2.5 sacks a game, tied 20th, and an 8.1 percent sack rate, 25th, with Ben Brown at right guard after Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten went to injured reserve.

The market and the site's models lean New England, with one dissent. ESPN and nflverse have the Patriots by 3.5 with a 45.5 total and at minus 192 on the money line, about 63 percent with the margin out; the ELO Model gives New England 58.9 percent and the Broly Model 63.1, the Joker takes Las Vegas at 50.5, and the power ratings have New England 6th at 1620 and Las Vegas 24th at 1422.

MIN-NO.note: Unbeaten Minnesota (4-0) is only a 1.5 point favorite at New Orleans (1-3): the league's stingiest scoring defense, 12.8 points a game, against a Saints offense that has scored at least 24 every week, with Justin Jefferson's ankle and two Vikings linemen the questions.
preview: Brian Flores' rush against a patched Saints line is the matchup. Minnesota gets 4.0 sacks a game, 1st, with Dallas Turner at 5.5, per nflverse, and pressures on 34.4 percent of dropbacks, 1st in the site's units; New Orleans allows 3.0 sacks a game, tied for 25th, with left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. on IR, per ESPN and Audacy, and Tyler Shough's strip sack started 4 straight turnovers against Las Vegas in Week 3, per ESPN and WWL.

Momentum is thin on both sides. Minnesota beat Miami 15-10 on five Will Reichard field goals and no touchdowns, and the site's ELO Ratings tab ranks Minnesota's Total Offense 27th; New Orleans lost 45-24 to Atlanta on Monday night, its second home loss in a row with 80 points allowed in the two, and Kellen Moore said they were not coaching or executing well enough, per Yahoo/SI and Canal Street Chronicles.

Something gives, and it is the Saints' scoring against the Vikings' defense. New Orleans has scored 30, 24, 27 and 24, converts 50 percent of third downs, 5th, and scores touchdowns on 80 percent of red zone trips, tied for 4th; Minnesota has allowed 22, 3, 16 and 10. The other side is softer: the Vikings average 4.4 yards a play, 32nd, against a defense allowing 32.0 points a game, 32nd.

The market barely leans and the site's models split. Minnesota is a 1.5 point favorite, minus 125 on nflverse's moneyline, with the total up from 41.5 Tuesday morning to 42.5 on ESPN's feed, about 22 to 20.5; the Joker (54.9 percent) and the Broly Model (54.1) take Minnesota, the ELO Model leans New Orleans at 50.3 percent, and the site's power ratings have the Vikings 5th and the Saints 28th. Wednesday afternoon's report on Justin Jefferson and Christian Darrisaw is what can move it.

CLE-NYJ.note: Cleveland, 3-1 and level with Baltimore atop the AFC North after three wins by a combined 10 points, visits a 1-3 Jets team that ran 32 plays in Chicago; New York is still the 2.5 point favorite, and the Browns play without Mason Graham.
preview: Cleveland's pass rush against the Jets' line is the matchup. The Jets allow 3.0 sacks a game, tied for 25th, and a 10.1 percent sack rate, 31st in the tracker, with Dylan Parham (knee) listed out as of Tuesday; Cleveland gets 3.0 sacks a game, tied for 5th, but Mason Graham (MCL and ankle sprains) likely misses Weeks 5 and 6, per NFL.com, Heavy and Yardbarker.

The streaks point opposite ways. Cleveland has won three straight by 4, 3 and 3 points, the last 27-24 over Pittsburgh on Andre Szmyt's 56 yard field goal with 10 seconds left, per ESPN and AP; the Jets have lost three straight, the last 23-12 in Chicago with a franchise low 32 offensive plays, per Yahoo, NBC and SNY.

Third down and turnovers should settle a low total. The 39.5 total is the week's second lowest, behind Houston at Tennessee; the Jets convert 32.0 percent of third downs, tied for 28th, and went 0 for 7 in Chicago, Cleveland 32.6 percent, 26th. New York is plus 0.8 in turnovers a game, tied for 4th, Cleveland minus 0.3, tied for 19th, and Geno Smith has no interceptions in 117 attempts, per nflverse.

The market and the site's models split. ESPN and nflverse have the Jets by 2.5, and nflverse's moneyline is minus 130, though the site's power ratings rank them 31st to Cleveland's 21st; the ELO Model (52.4 percent) and the Broly Model (53.4) take New York, and the Joker takes Cleveland at 55.1 percent.

IND-PIT.note: Two 2-2 teams in Pittsburgh: Indianapolis back from a 30-13 London win over Washington, Pittsburgh on 10 days' rest after a 27-24 loss in Cleveland, with Daniel Jones's 7 giveaways meeting T.J. Watt and a Steelers secondary that traded Joey Porter Jr. and lost Jamel Dean to an ankle.
preview: T.J. Watt against Daniel Jones's grip on the ball is the matchup. Jones has 4 interceptions and 3 fumbles lost on sacks in four games, per nflverse, including an interception and a lost fumble in London, per AP; Indianapolis is minus 1.5 a game in turnover margin, 32nd. Watt has 4.5 sacks, per nflverse, and Pittsburgh's secondary ends 18.1 percent of dropbacks with an interception or a pass defensed, 3rd in the site's units.

Momentum runs opposite ways. Indianapolis has won two straight, 19-17 over Houston and 30-13 over Washington; Pittsburgh lost 27-24 in Cleveland on Andre Szmyt's 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left, per ESPN and AP, then spent the week on Mike McCarthy's viral sideline exchange with Aaron Rodgers, per Athlon and PFN, while Joey Porter Jr. was traded to Dallas, per the Cowboys' site, KDKA and TSN.

Finishing drives is the winning factor. Indianapolis averages 25.5 points, 13th, on 4.5 yards a play, tied for 30th, because it scores touchdowns on 75 percent of red zone trips, 6th, and Spencer Shrader is 11 for 11 on field goals; Pittsburgh scores touchdowns on 44.4 percent, tied for 28th, has no rushing touchdown this season, per nflverse, and Chris Boswell is 7 for 10.

The market and the site's models lean Pittsburgh. The Steelers are 2.5 point favorites with a 44.5 total in ESPN's feed and nflverse's lines, an implied 23.5 to 21; the Joker (57.5 percent), the Broly Model (57.2) and the ELO Model (55.2) all take Pittsburgh, which is 14th in the site's power rank to Indianapolis's 19th.

NYG-WAS.note: A division game in Landover: 3-1 New York, alone in first in the NFC East, is a 3 to 3.5 point underdog at 1-3 Washington, where Jayden Daniels aims to return from a dislocated left elbow after Marcus Mariota sprained his right MCL in a 30-13 loss to Indianapolis in London.
preview: Washington's run game against the Giants' front is the matchup. The Commanders run for 124 yards a game, 8th, per nflverse, behind a line 8th in the site's unit grades, and Jayden Daniels ran 12 times for 100 yards in his two games; New York allows 4.7 yards a carry, 25th, its front grades 32nd in the site's units, and it has 3 sacks in four games, 0.8 a game, 32nd.

The teams arrive going opposite ways. New York beat Arizona 36-24, sealed by Deonte Banks' 98-yard pick-six, per Giants.com and NFL.com, its second outright win as an underdog; Washington lost 30-13 to Indianapolis in London, lost Marcus Mariota (right MCL sprain) on the second drive and Jaylin Lane for the season, is 0-2 in the division, and Dan Quinn turned up on post-Week 4 hot seat lists.

Turnovers could swing it. Both teams are plus 0.8 a game in turnover margin, tied 4th; New York's 6 interceptions are tied with Seattle and Jacksonville for the league lead and its secondary gets a hand on 19.5 percent of dropbacks, 1st in the site's unit numbers, while Washington has 2 giveaways, tied for 3rd fewest, and Daniels and Mariota have 7 touchdown passes and no interceptions in 102 attempts, per nflverse. Jameis Winston threw 2 interceptions in Week 4.

The market and the site's models take Washington. The Commanders are 3.5 point favorites in ESPN's line (3 in the Oct 6 pull) and nflverse's, with a 43.5 total, an implied 23.5 to 20, and the Joker (52.4 percent), the Broly Model (59.2) and the ELO Model (70.5, projecting Daniels at quarterback) all pick Washington; on the other side, the Giants are 3-1 against the spread in nflverse's lines and rank 23rd in the site's power rank to Washington's 27th.

DEN-LAC.note: An AFC West game at SoFi: Denver, 2-2 and a 3.5 point favorite after a 24-14 loss in San Francisco, likely without Pat Surtain II, against an 0-4 Chargers team that lost Rashawn Slater for 4 to 6 weeks and finished in Seattle with four rookie linemen.
preview: Denver's rush against a Chargers line of rookies is the matchup. Rashawn Slater has a high ankle sprain and is out 4 to 6 weeks, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Joe Alt (neck) is still being evaluated, and the Chargers finished in Seattle with four rookie linemen, per Chargers.com and PFT. Justin Herbert has been sacked 12 times, tied for 3rd most, per nflverse; Zach Allen has 12 quarterback hits, 3rd in the NFL, though Denver did not sack Brock Purdy on Sunday.

Both teams come off losses, one far deeper. Denver lost 24-14 at San Francisco after Marvin Mims Jr.'s muffed punt set up the go-ahead touchdown, per AP and PFT, and is 0-2 on the road. The Chargers are 0-4, every loss by 7 or more, though their 23 points in a 30-23 loss at Seattle were a season high; Jim Harbaugh, 2nd on post-Week 4 hot seat lists per SportsGrid and Yahoo, says he is "treating it like it's a one-game season," per Chargers.com.

Turnovers could decide it. The Chargers have 10 giveaways in four games, tied with New England for the most, per nflverse: Herbert's 6 interceptions, tied for 2nd most, and 4 lost fumbles, with 4 giveaways at Seattle alone; they are minus 0.8 a game in turnover margin, tied for 24th, per TeamRankings. Denver has 5 giveaways and Bo Nix threw none Sunday; its 4 interceptions on defense are tied for 4th, but none came at San Francisco and Pat Surtain II was listed doubtful as of Tuesday, per ESPN.

The market and the site's models all take Denver. The Broncos are 3.5 point favorites with a 42.5 total in ESPN's feed and nflverse's lines, minus 185 on nflverse's moneyline, an implied 23 to 19.5; the Broly Model (64.2 percent), the Joker (56.0) and the ELO Model (53.9) agree, and Denver is 8th in the site's power rank to the Chargers' 25th. Six of the two teams' eight games have gone under the closing total, per nflverse.

DET-ARI.note: Detroit (2-2) has allowed 30 or more points in three of four games and is a 4.5 to 5.5 point road favorite at Arizona (1-3), which lost left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. for the season and expects Jeremiyah Love to sit; the 54.5 total ties Bills at Rams for the highest of the week.
preview: Jared Goff against Arizona's pass defense is the matchup. Goff has 1,214 yards, 9 touchdowns and no interceptions on 161 attempts, per nflverse, and ranks 3rd at 0.23 EPA a dropback in the site's unit numbers; Arizona allows 0.23 EPA a dropback there, 31st, 6.1 yards a play, 30th, and has given up 11 touchdown passes, tied with Detroit and Washington for the most.

Both lost as road favorites in Week 4. Detroit fell 32-26 at Carolina on Sunday night despite Goff's 412 yards, as Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 for 192 and 2 touchdowns, per ESPN and Panthers.com; Arizona lost 36-24 at the Giants, its third straight loss, sealed by Deonte Banks' 98-yard interception return, per Giants.com and NFL.com.

Detroit's leaky secondary against the league's least explosive passing game decides how close it gets. The Lions allow 327 passing yards a game, 32nd, and have given up 20 completions of 20 or more yards, the most, per nflverse, with Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) expected out, per The Detroit News; Arizona has 4 such completions all season, the fewest, and 1.3 explosive plays a game, 32nd.

The market and the site's models all take Detroit. ESPN's line has the Lions by 4.5 and nflverse's by 5.5, at minus 258 on the moneyline, with a 54.5 total; the ELO Model (71.8 percent), the Joker (81.7) and the Broly Model (68.9) all pick Detroit, and the site's power rank has the Lions 13th and the Cardinals 29th.

SF-SEA.note: Unbeaten San Francisco, 1st in yards per play and still without a sack allowed, makes its first true road trip of the season to the defending champion Seahawks, 1st in yards per play allowed, who beat the 49ers 41-6 at Lumen Field in January; Nick Bosa is not expected to play.
preview: The league's best offense meets its best defense. San Francisco leads the NFL in yards per play (6.8), third down rate (57.5 percent) and red zone touchdown rate (84.6 percent) and is the only team without a sack allowed, per TeamRankings; Seattle allows 4.0 yards a play, 1st, and 18.3 points a game, 5th, with 11 sacks, 7th, and 6 interceptions, tied for 1st, per nflverse. In the last two meetings Seattle held the 49ers to 9 points and sacked Brock Purdy 5 times.

Momentum favors San Francisco, the recent history Seattle. The 49ers beat Denver 24-14 with touchdowns on three straight second half drives and 1 penalty for 5 yards, per AP, PFT and nflverse; Seattle beat the Chargers 30-23 with 4 takeaways but 14 penalties for a franchise record 150 yards, per ESPN and the Spokesman-Review. Seattle won the last two meetings 13-3 and 41-6, and a win Sunday ties the NFC West at 4-1.

The winning factor is Seattle's passing game against a 49ers rush without Nick Bosa. Bosa, out the last two games, and James Thompson Jr. (ankle) are not expected to play, per Kyle Shanahan to the Mercury News and ESPN, and safety Marques Sigle is out for multiple weeks, per The Athletic and ESPN; San Francisco has 6 sacks, tied for 26th, none against Denver. Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 6 touchdown catches and has 481 yards, 3rd, per nflverse.

The market and the site's models split. Seattle is a 2.5 to 3 point favorite at minus 155 with a 46.5 to 47.5 total, per ESPN and nflverse; the Broly Model takes Seattle at 55.0 percent, while the Joker (50.7 percent) and the ELO Model (51.6 percent) take San Francisco. The site's power rank has Seattle 1st and San Francisco 2nd, the top two meeting.

BAL-ATL.note: Sunday night in Atlanta: 3-1 Baltimore probably without Lamar Jackson, whose ankle sprain puts Tyler Huntley in line to start, against a 2-2 Falcons team scoring 40 a game since Michael Penix Jr. returned and playing for sole possession of first in the NFC South while Carolina is on bye.
preview: Baltimore's run game against the league's best run defense is the matchup. Atlanta allows 48.3 rushing yards a game and 2.7 a carry, both 1st, and has not given up a 20 yard run, per nflverse; Fox had the Falcons at 47.7 a game through three weeks. Derrick Henry has 374 yards and 7 touchdowns at 4.2 a carry, and without Lamar Jackson (19 carries, 144 yards) the Ravens lose the quarterback run that sets it up.

Atlanta has the momentum, Baltimore has the injury list. The Falcons won 35-14 at Green Bay and 45-24 at New Orleans in Penix's two starts, with 447 rushing yards and 1 turnover, after 16 points and 7 giveaways in two losses, per NFL.com, AP and nflverse. Baltimore beat 0-4 Tennessee only 24-18 as an 11.5 point favorite, finished it without Jackson (ankle) and lost Durham Smythe (Achilles) for the season.

Something gives when Atlanta makes Baltimore throw. Opponents run 17.8 times a game against the Falcons, so the 276.5 passing yards a game they allow, 29th, come at 6.2 yards an attempt, 4th, per nflverse. Baltimore's 9.8 yards an attempt, 1st, is Jackson's number; Tyler Huntley went 8 of 9 for 63 yards in relief Sunday, per ESPN's feed and nflverse.

The market moved to Atlanta, and the site's models split. Atlanta went from 1.5 to 3 point favorites on ESPN's feed Tuesday and was at 3.5, minus 175 on the moneyline, total 43.5, on nflverse Wednesday. The site's Joker (62.2 percent) and Broly Model (61.5) take Atlanta; the ELO Model takes Baltimore at 63.3 percent, but it still has Jackson in its lineup. The site's power ratings have the Ravens 11th and the Falcons 17th.

BUF-LAR.note: 3-1 Buffalo, off its first loss, 29-26 to New England, visits 2-2 Los Angeles on Monday night; the Rams are 2.5 to 3 point favorites, and the 54.5 total, tied for the week's highest, pits the league's top scoring offense against the defense allowing the fewest passing yards.
preview: Buffalo's offense against the Rams' pass defense is the matchup. The Bills lead the league at 31.8 points a game and 5.5 plays of 20 or more yards a game, and Josh Allen has 13 touchdowns, 6 passing and 7 rushing, per nflverse; the Rams allow 153.8 passing yards a game, 1st, and 4.2 yards a play, 2nd, with Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake at 7 passes defensed each.

Both come off fourth quarter finishes, in opposite directions. Buffalo lost 29-26 to New England as a 7 point favorite, its first loss under Joe Brady, on Efton Chism III's 23 yard touchdown with 1:55 left, per ESPN and Pro Football Talk; the Rams won 24-20 at Philadelphia from 20-10 down on two Kyren Williams touchdown runs in the last 3:59, per Eagles.com, PFT and CBS.

The Rams have to turn yards into touchdowns. Los Angeles gains 417.0 yards a game, 2nd, but scores 21.3, 19th, with touchdowns on 53.3 percent of red zone trips, tied 21st, and a turnover margin of minus 1.3 a game, tied 27th; Buffalo scores touchdowns on 68.8 percent of trips, 9th, and has 10 rushing touchdowns, the most, while the Rams have allowed 1, tied for 2nd fewest.

The market and the site's models lean Rams, narrowly. ESPN has Los Angeles by 2.5 and nflverse by 3, both with a 54.5 total, and the money line is Rams minus 162, about 59 percent with the margin out; the Broly Model gives the Rams 58.9 percent, the Joker 53.0 and the ELO Model 50.9, while the power ratings have Buffalo 3rd at 1667 and the Rams 7th at 1614.

TB.headline: 0-4, a rookie's first road start, and four players ruled out
matchup: Tampa Bay is an 8.5 to 10 point road underdog. The line opened at 9.5, per Covers, and is 10 at ESPN and SI and 8.5 in the consensus line Wednesday morning, with a 47.5 total; Pete Prisco has Dallas 34-14 and ESPN's FPI gives the Bucs 13 percent, while Covers' Jason Logan leans to Tampa Bay with the points.

The decider is Jalon Daniels against the league's worst pass defense. Dallas allows 6.4 yards a play, 32nd, and 0.34 EPA per dropback, 32nd in the tracker, and Houston scored 30 on it Sunday; Daniels threw for 148 yards on 27 attempts in his debut, 5.5 a throw, with 2 interceptions.

Everything around the quarterback works against them. A short week, a first road start in prime time, and Todd Bowles ruled out Baker Mayfield, Antoine Winfield Jr., Benjamin Morrison and SirVocea Dennis on Wednesday, per SI and Bucs Report, though kicker Chase McLaughlin (groin, hip) will play, per PFT and the Tampa Bay Times; Bowles tops the hot seat lists, per PFT and Pro Football Network, and only the 1992 Chargers have made the playoffs after 0-4.
strengths: The run defense is elite. Runners gain 1.73 yards after contact a carry, the league's lowest, per the Bucs' site, and 3.2 a carry overall, per SI; the front is 2nd in rush EPA allowed in the tracker, with Vita Vea in the middle.

They keep every game close. Losses of 6, 4, 7 and 3 points, ending with 17-14 to Green Bay, and 10 straight one score games, the longest streak in team history and the longest active in the NFL, per the Bucs' site; the defense allows 5.0 yards a play, tied for 6th.

Jalon Daniels runs, and Dallas cannot stop quarterbacks who do. His 55 rushing yards on 8 carries against Green Bay set a Bucs rookie quarterback record, per AP and the Bucs' site, after 1,445 rushing yards and 23 touchdowns at Kansas; Dallas has allowed a league high 188 rushing yards to quarterbacks, per Sharp.
Bucky Irving gets a soft run defense. 16 carries for 61 yards Sunday, and the backs rank 8th in rush EPA per carry in the tracker; Dallas is 26th in rush EPA allowed and its run defense ranks 28th.

Rueben Bain Jr. is back. Inactive for Week 4 with groin and shoulder injuries, he was a full participant Monday and Tuesday, per the Bucs' site and the official report, and Bowles said Wednesday he will play, per the Tampa Bay Times and SI; Josiah Trotter (knee) went from limited Monday to full Tuesday.
weaknesses: Baker Mayfield is out again. The dislocated right thumb carries a 3 to 6 week timeline, per Schefter; an MRI showed no added ligament or tendon damage, he is not on injured reserve, and his return depends on when he can grip the ball, per ESPN and NBC. He did not practice Monday or Tuesday.

The back seven is thin. Antoine Winfield Jr. has a slight rib fracture and is out 2 to 4 weeks, per Bowles and ESPN; Benjamin Morrison (quad) and SirVocea Dennis (ankle, foot) missed practice Monday and Tuesday and were ruled out Wednesday, per SI and Bucs Report.

The offense cannot protect or finish. 4.0 sacks allowed a game, the most in the NFL, and touchdowns on 41.7 percent of red zone trips, 31st; 19.0 points a game, tied 24th, and 14 in Sunday's 17-14 loss to Green Bay.

The blitz is not getting home. Tampa Bay blitzes 40.4 percent of dropbacks, 3rd, but pressures on 24.6 percent, 31st, per Sharp, and 19.0 percent, 27th, in the tracker; 1.5 sacks a game ranks tied 26th, against a Dallas line allowing 1.5 a game, tied 5th.
keys: Win the turnover battle. Tampa Bay is minus 1.3 a game, tied 27th, and Jalon Daniels' two first half interceptions Sunday turned into 10 Green Bay points; Dallas has no interceptions in four games, so a clean game from Daniels keeps it close.

Run the quarterback and Bucky Irving. Dallas has allowed a league high 188 rushing yards to quarterbacks, per Sharp, and ranks 28th against the run in the tracker; designed runs for Daniels and a steady dose of Irving shorten the game against an offense scoring 30.5 a game, tied 2nd.

Make Dallas kick. The Cowboys score touchdowns on 81.3 percent of red zone trips, 3rd, and Javonte Williams ran for 3 Sunday; a run defense allowing 1.73 yards after contact can stall him short, and Brandon Aubrey went 2 of 4 in Houston.

DAL.headline: Lamb's record night, a last ranked pass defense, and Tyler Smith nearly back
matchup: Dallas is an 8.5 to 10 point home favorite. The line opened at 9.5, per Covers, with a 47.5 total and Dallas about -455 on the moneyline; Pete Prisco has the Cowboys 34-14 and ESPN's FPI makes them 87 percent winners by 11.4, while Covers' Jason Logan leans to the Bucs with the points and SI takes the Over.

The deciding matchup is CeeDee Lamb against a thinned secondary. Lamb leads the NFL with 37 catches and 498 yards; Tampa Bay is without Antoine Winfield Jr. (ribs) and Benjamin Morrison (quad), both ruled out Wednesday, per SI and Bucs Report, and the pass defense ranks 18th in EPA allowed per dropback in the tracker.

The defense and the calendar work against them. 28.0 points allowed a game, 28th, with 4 sacks and no interceptions in four games, per the Bucs' site; this Thursday game follows Rio in Week 3 and Houston in Week 4 with no bye between, though both teams are on 4 days' rest.
strengths: The offense scores with anyone. 30.5 points a game, tied 2nd, 51.0 percent on third down, 4th, and touchdowns on 81.3 percent of red zone trips, 3rd; Dak Prescott has 1,065 yards and 8 touchdowns, per Bucs Nation, and ranks 2nd at 0.24 EPA per dropback.

CeeDee Lamb set the team receiver record. 17 catches on 21 targets for 189 yards and the 12 yard winner with 40 seconds left in Houston, the most catches by a Cowboys wide receiver, per CBS and the Dallas Morning News; only Jason Witten has had more in a game.

The line protects, and Tyler Smith may return. Dallas allows 1.5 sacks a game, tied 5th, and a 4.3 percent sack rate, 4th in the tracker; the All-Pro left guard, on injured reserve since thumb surgery, was limited Monday and Tuesday, and Brian Schottenheimer says he plays if he says he is ready, per the Dallas Morning News and ESPN.
They came back in Houston. Down 16-6 at halftime, Dallas won 34-30; Javonte Williams ran for a career high 3 touchdowns, all after halftime, and Prescott went 32 of 45 for 335 yards, per CBS and AP.

Joey Porter Jr. steadies the corners. Acquired from Pittsburgh for a 2028 2nd, a 2027 6th and a conditional 6th, he played 25 defensive snaps in his debut, per NFL.com, and was a full participant Tuesday.
weaknesses: The pass defense ranks last. 6.4 yards a play allowed, 32nd, and 0.34 EPA per dropback, 32nd in the tracker; Houston scored 30 on it Sunday and Baltimore 34 in Rio the week before.

No pass rush and no takeaways. 4 sacks in four games, 1.0 a game, tied 28th, and no interceptions, per the Bucs' site; interceptions plus passes defended come on 7.9 percent of dropbacks, 32nd in the tracker.

The defense is still short handed. Cobie Durant (hamstring) is expected to miss Thursday, per the Cowboys' site, and DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) is a long shot, per Schottenheimer; both, and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), did not practice Monday or Tuesday, and Jalen Thompson and Jonathan Bullard are on injured reserve.

The run game is ordinary. Javonte Williams needed 19 carries for 62 yards in Houston, 3.3 a carry, despite his 3 touchdowns; the backs average 4.2 a carry, 15th in the tracker, against a Tampa Bay front 2nd in rush EPA allowed.
Special teams keep leaking. Brandon Aubrey went 2 of 4 on field goals in Houston, per CBS and ESPN, with Will Anderson Jr. blocking a 62 yard try.
keys: Feed CeeDee Lamb early. 21 targets Sunday and an NFL best 498 yards, against a secondary without Antoine Winfield Jr. and Benjamin Morrison, both ruled out, and likely playing Ifeatu Melifonwu at safety.

Keep Jalon Daniels in the pocket. Dallas has allowed a league high 188 rushing yards to quarterbacks, per Sharp, and Daniels ran for 55 Sunday; make him throw, where he averaged 5.5 yards an attempt with 2 interceptions, and get the defense's first pick of the year.

Beat the blitz. Tampa Bay blitzes 40.4 percent of dropbacks, 3rd, but gets pressure on 24.6 percent, 31st, per Sharp; Dak Prescott, 2nd at 0.24 EPA per dropback, behind a line allowing 1.5 sacks a game and possibly Tyler Smith back at left guard, can punish it.

PHI.headline: Two straight losses, Lane Johnson retired, Cam Jurgens traded, and two healthy running backs
matchup: Philadelphia is a 6.5 to 7 point underdog in London. The line opened near 4.5, per Covers and SI, and was 5.5 on Monday, per the Inquirer; Pete Prisco (Jaguars 28-16), Tyler Sullivan (30-17), SI, Covers and Bleacher Report all pick Jacksonville, and it is the Eagles' second straight week as an underdog after the Rams were 3 point favorites.

The decider is the rebuilt offensive line. Lane Johnson retired Tuesday and Landon Dickerson (knee) is on injured reserve until Week 6 at the earliest, per the Inquirer, PFT and NBC Sports Philadelphia, and left guard Cam Jurgens was traded to Baltimore Wednesday, per the Inquirer and Pro Football Rumors; rookie Markel Bell stays at right tackle after the Rams' Byron Young had 2.5 sacks in his first start, per NFL.com.

Working against them is a skill group without its stars. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is week to week, per NFL Network, ESPN and PFT, and the Inquirer hears he is unlikely to play; DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dallas Goedert (knee) and Marquise Brown (ankle) missed Week 4 and were still listed out on ESPN's feed as of Tuesday, against a Jaguars run defense 3rd and secondary 4th in the tracker.
strengths: The pass defense is sound. The secondary ranks 9th in the tracker and 8th in pass EPA allowed, and Philadelphia gives up 5.2 yards a play, tied 12th; Quinyon Mitchell's knee injury from Sunday is not considered serious after Monday's tests, per NFL Network and the Liberty Line.

The defense held the Rams to 10 points for 56 minutes. Philadelphia led 20-10 in the fourth quarter before Kyren Williams scored with 3:59 and 1:10 left, per Eagles.com, PFT and CBS; the Rams came in leading the league in yards a game, per NFL.com.

Darius Cooper is a red zone answer. Both of Jalen Hurts' touchdown passes against the Rams went to Cooper in the first half (3 catches, 33 yards), per ESPN and NBC Sports Philadelphia, and the Eagles score touchdowns on 61.5 percent of red zone trips, 13th.
They keep games close. Three of four have been decided by 4 points or fewer: 24-22 over Washington, 24-20 at Tennessee and the 24-20 loss to the Rams; only the 27-7 loss at Chicago got away.
weaknesses: The offense vanished in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. 172 total yards, 68 net passing yards and no points after halftime, per Yahoo, CBS and NBC Sports Philadelphia; Jalen Hurts went 12 of 27 for 93 yards, 10 of them after the break, and blamed poor execution. Philadelphia scores 18.8 points a game, 26th, and has not topped 24 in any game.

Lane Johnson and Cam Jurgens are gone. The right tackle retired Tuesday at 36, four weeks into his 14th season, citing mental health and family, per the Inquirer, PFT and Eagles.com; Jordan Mailata said he is still kinda shocked. A day later the left guard, in the concussion protocol since Monday, went to Baltimore with a 2027 7th for a 2027 5th and a 2028 2nd, per the Inquirer and Pro Football Rumors. The line already allows 3 sacks a game, tied 25th, and an 8 percent sack rate, 24th in the tracker.

The backfield is down to Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce. Saquon Barkley hurt his hamstring four snaps into Sunday's game, and Tank Bigsby went to injured reserve Tuesday ahead of core muscle surgery, per ESPN, the Inquirer and Eagles.com, leaving Shipley (6 carries, 23 yards Sunday) as the only healthy back on the 53 until Pierce was promoted from the practice squad Wednesday, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and PFT.

The receivers are thin and stuck. With DeVonta Smith and Marquise Brown listed out, Dontayvion Wicks (3 catches, 18 yards) and rookie Makai Lemon (3 for 27) were the other wideouts beside Darius Cooper on Sunday, per ESPN; the receiving unit ranks 30th in the tracker, with 3.9 yards after the catch, 32nd.

The pass rush and the takeaways are missing. 1 sack a game, tied 28th, an 18.4 percent pressure rate, 28th in the tracker, and minus 0.8 in turnovers a game, tied 24th; Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is day to day and Zack Baun (concussion), out in Week 4, was still listed out as of Tuesday, per NFL Network and ESPN.
keys: Protect Hurts with a patched line. Help rookie Markel Bell at right tackle and, with Cam Jurgens traded, likely first time starter Willie Lampkin at left guard against a Jaguars front with 2.5 sacks a game, tied 8th; the ball has to come out on time.

Stay level before halftime. Jacksonville has outscored opponents 61-9 before halftime and has not allowed a first half touchdown in 20 possessions, per the USA Today Network; Philadelphia scored all 20 of its points before halftime against the Rams, so it needs a second half too.

Win the turnover battle. Jacksonville is plus 1.5 a game, 1st, and Philadelphia minus 0.8, tied 24th; Trevor Lawrence has 2 interceptions in four games, so Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell have to cash the few chances they get.

JAX.headline: 3-1, the No. 2 scoring defense, and the first of two London home games
matchup: Jacksonville is a 6.5 to 7 point favorite at Tottenham. Up from about 4.5 early in the week, per Covers and SI; Pete Prisco has the Jaguars 28-16, Tyler Sullivan 30-17 and covering, and ESPN's FPI gives them about 73 percent. Covers and PredictEm lean Under.

The decider is Trevor Lawrence against a quiet pass rush. Lawrence has 843 yards, 8 touchdowns and 2 interceptions, per the USA Today Network and CBS, and the quarterback unit is 6th in EPA per dropback in the tracker; Philadelphia has 1 sack a game, tied 28th, and edge Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is day to day.

Working against them is the secondary's health. Eric Murray was still in the concussion protocol as of Tuesday after leaving the Cincinnati game, and Montaric Brown (hamstring) missed Week 4, per SI and CBS; Travis Hunter played every defensive snap and none on offense to cover for it, per PFT and Jaguars.com.
strengths: The defense allows 13.3 points a game, 2nd. Prisco leans on it in his pick; the run defense ranks 3rd in the tracker and Covers has Jacksonville allowing the 3rd fewest yards a rush, a bad fit for an Eagles team down to Will Shipley and the just promoted Dameon Pierce at running back.

They finish drives. 51.1 percent on third down, 3rd, and touchdowns on 81.8 percent of red zone trips, 2nd, the numbers CBS's Tyler Sullivan leads with when he calls Jacksonville the best team in the AFC right now.

Lawrence finally beat Cincinnati. He went 18 of 23 for 227 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions in the 22-17 win at Cincinnati, his first in four tries against the Bengals, per AP and ESPN; Brenton Strange caught 7 of 8 targets for 95 yards.

They bury teams early. A 61-9 first half scoring margin, the league's best, and no first half touchdown allowed in 20 possessions, per the USA Today Network preview; Sharp had the margin at 48-6 before Week 4.
They win the turnover battle. Plus 1.5 a game, 1st; Travis Hunter broke up 2 passes at Cincinnati and had an interception wiped out by a roughing call on Arik Armstead, per Jaguars.com and ESPN.
weaknesses: The defensive backfield is being restocked. Safety Caleb Ransaw (knee) went to injured reserve Monday for the second straight season and corner Christian Braswell (knee) was waived injured; Jacksonville signed corners Alijah Huzzie (off Houston's practice squad) and Jaylon Jones, per Big Cat Country, Black and Teal and RotoWire.

Penalties nearly cost them the Cincinnati game. 13 for 125 yards, 10 for 100 in the first half, per the Alligator and AP; a holding call erased Bhayshul Tuten's 44 yard touchdown run, and he finished with 73 yards on 17 carries.

Yards come against them. Jacksonville allows 5.9 yards a play, tied 27th, despite giving up only 13.3 points; Action News Jax calls the defense situational masters, which leaves little room if third downs and the red zone turn.

The offensive line and big plays are middling. The line ranks 20th in the tracker with a 6.9 percent sack rate, 19th, and 4.1 yards a carry, 20th, and the offense has 3.3 explosive plays a game, tied 18th.
keys: Load up against the run and make Hurts throw. Saquon Barkley is week to week and Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce, promoted Wednesday, are the only healthy backs; the Rams shut Philadelphia out after halftime and held Jalen Hurts to 10 passing yards in the second half.

Test the rookie at right tackle. Markel Bell makes his second start with Lane Johnson retired, Josh Hines-Allen has a sack in four straight games, per CBS, and Philadelphia, which traded left guard Cam Jurgens Wednesday, allows 3 sacks a game, tied 25th.

Play clean. 13 penalties for 125 yards wiped out two touchdowns and an interception at Cincinnati; an Eagles offense coming off 0 for 12 on third down needs free yards to move, so do not hand them any.

CHI.headline: Bagent gets Lambeau, and the Bears are 2-0 without Caleb Williams
matchup: Chicago is a 3 point road favorite. The total is 45.5 and the Bears are about -148 on the moneyline, per ESPN's line and the consensus line; CBS's Pete Prisco picks the Packers in an upset, while the site's power ratings put Chicago 9th and Green Bay 18th.

The run game against a Packers front without Edgerrin Cooper decides it. The line ranks 2nd and the backs average 4.9 a carry, 4th; Green Bay is 23rd in rush EPA allowed per carry and lost Cooper (Achilles) for the season, per Packers.com and Rapoport.

Working against them is the red zone. Touchdowns on 42.1 percent of trips, 30th; Cairo Santos kicked 3 field goals in the 23-12 win over the Jets, per ESPN, and field goals leave a 3 point favorite little room at Lambeau.
strengths: The backups are 2-0. Case Keenum beat Philadelphia 27-7 in Week 3, and Tyson Bagent beat the Jets 23-12 in his first start since his 2023 rookie year, 25 of 34 for 268 yards, per the Sun-Times and WGN.
The defense smothered the Jets. 32 offensive plays, a Jets franchise low, 4 in the first quarter and 0 for 7 on third down, per Yahoo, NBC and SNY; Chicago allows 16.3 points a game, 4th.

The line protects and opens holes. It ranks 2nd, with a 4.5 percent sack rate allowed, 5th, and 1.8 sacks a game, tied 10th fewest; the backs average 4.9 a carry, 4th, and D'Andre Swift ran 15 times for 58 yards Sunday, per ESPN.

Bagent's targets made plays. Rome Odunze caught 6 for 94 yards, Colston Loveland 6 for 57 on 9 targets and Luther Burden III 4 for 63 against the Jets, per ESPN; Chicago has 4.8 plays of 20 or more yards a game, tied 3rd, and converts 47.4 percent on third down, 6th.

Green Bay's defense keeps losing players. Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles) is out for the season, Micah Parsons (ACL) will not practice this week and Warren Brinson (calf, groin) went on injured reserve Saturday, per Packers.com, SI, Yahoo and PFR.
weaknesses: Caleb Williams misses a third straight game. Ben Johnson said Monday the grade 2 hamstring keeps him out of practice all week and he is still week to week, per ESPN's Courtney Cronin, the Sun-Times and PFT; Case Keenum backs up Bagent, per the Tribune.
The run defense is the soft spot. 27th in rush EPA allowed per carry and 31st in the tracker's run defense ranking; the front ranks 23rd, and the defense allows 5.9 yards a play, tied 27th.
Ball security slipped Sunday. Bagent threw an interception, per the Sun-Times and WGN, and D'Andre Swift lost a fumble, per ESPN; Chicago is plus 0.3 a game in turnover margin, tied 14th.

The injury list is long. Tackle Braxton Jones (knee) went on injured reserve Saturday, per NFL.com and RotoWire; Kyle Monangai (right thumb) is day to day, per the Sun-Times, and questionable on ESPN's feed as of Tuesday; Kyler Gordon (calf), still on the reserve list Wednesday morning, was ruled out of Week 4 and Cam Lewis (hip) was doubtful, per the official report, and both are listed out on ESPN's feed as of Tuesday.
The only division game was a 9-3 loss. Minnesota held Chicago to 3 points at Soldier Field in Week 2, and the Bears trail the 4-0 Vikings by a game in the NFC North.
keys: Run at the hole Cooper left. D'Andre Swift and, if the thumb allows, Kyle Monangai behind a line ranked 2nd, against a Green Bay defense 23rd in rush EPA allowed; it keeps Tyson Bagent out of third and long.

Turn red zone trips into touchdowns. Chicago scores touchdowns on 42.1 percent of trips, 30th, and settled for 3 Cairo Santos field goals Sunday; Green Bay is barely better at 46.7 percent, 27th, so finishing drives is the edge.

Win third down on defense again. The Jets went 0 for 7 on Sunday, per Yahoo and SNY; Green Bay converts 26.1 percent, last in the league, so stopping the run on early downs puts Jordan Love where the Packers fail.

GB.headline: A home underdog without Edgerrin Cooper, and still last on third down
matchup: Green Bay is a 3 point home underdog. The total is 45.5 and the Packers are about +124 on the moneyline; CBS's Pete Prisco picks them in an upset, but Green Bay lost its only home game, 35-14 to Atlanta in Week 3.

The run game against Chicago's run defense decides it. Green Bay's backs are 31st in rush EPA per carry and average 3.8 yards a carry, 29th; Chicago is 27th in rush EPA allowed and 31st in the tracker's run defense ranking. MarShawn Lloyd ran 7 times for 13 yards at Tampa and Kaleb Johnson 8 for 42, per ESPN, after starter Chris Brooks left in the first half with an ankle injury that was still being tested Monday, per SI and NBC Sports.
Working against them is third down. 26.1 percent, 32nd, against a Chicago defense that held the Jets 0 for 7 on Sunday, per Yahoo, NBC and SNY; Green Bay scores 18.3 points a game, 28th.
strengths: Jordan Love was efficient at Tampa. 22 of 30 for 197 yards and 2 touchdowns, to Tucker Kraft and Matthew Golden, per ESPN, in the 17-14 win; he ranks 10th in EPA per dropback at 0.11.
The defense took the ball away. Jalon Daniels' two first half interceptions led to 10 Green Bay points, per the AP and the Bucs' site; the Packers allow 5.0 yards a play, tied 6th.
The pass rush can get home. 2.5 sacks a game, tied 8th, and pressure on 25.5 percent of dropbacks, 10th, against Tyson Bagent in his second straight start.

The receivers stretch the field. The group ranks 9th, with 9.9 percent of throws gaining 20 or more yards, 10th; Christian Watson caught all 3 targets for 47 yards Sunday, per ESPN, and Chicago allows 5.9 yards a play, tied 27th.
Love stays upright. A 5.2 percent sack rate allowed, 7th, even with Aaron Banks (toe) and Jacob Monk (quad) out in Week 4; Chicago's front ranks 23rd.
weaknesses: Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season. He tore his Achilles at Tampa and went on injured reserve Tuesday, and Kristian Welch was promoted from the practice squad, per Packers.com, Ian Rapoport and PFR.

Micah Parsons is not close. Matt LaFleur said Monday he will not practice this week as he works back from his 2025 torn ACL, per Packers.com's Weston Hodkiewicz; SI and Yahoo say his return could come in November.

The interior is thin on both lines. Warren Brinson (calf, groin) went on injured reserve Saturday, per NFL.com and PFR; Anthony Campbell (ankle), Aaron Banks (toe) and Jacob Monk (quad) were out in Week 4, per the official report, and are still listed out on ESPN's feed as of Tuesday.

The run game is 31st. 3.8 yards a carry, 29th, and minus 0.15 rush EPA per carry, 31st, in the tracker, and Josh Jacobs is still on the Commissioner's Exempt List in the league's roster data as of Wednesday morning, as he was last week, per ESPN.

Turnovers nearly cost them at Tampa. FOX11 and Yahoo say the Packers survived two fourth quarter turnovers; Love threw an interception and Kaleb Johnson lost a fumble, per ESPN, and Green Bay is minus 0.5 a game in turnover margin, tied 21st.
keys: Hold up against the run without Cooper. Chicago's line ranks 2nd and its backs average 4.9 a carry, 4th; Green Bay is 23rd in rush EPA allowed, and the linebackers have to cover for Edgerrin Cooper.

Put Tyson Bagent in third and long. Chicago converts 47.4 percent on third down, 6th; the Packers' 2.5 sacks a game, tied 8th, have to come without Micah Parsons against a line allowing a 4.5 percent sack rate, 5th.

Run it, and hold onto it. Chicago's run defense ranks 31st in the tracker, a chance for MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson to lift a run game that is 31st in rush EPA; Green Bay is minus 0.5 a game in turnover margin, tied 21st, and cannot give it away twice in the fourth quarter again.

HOU.headline: 0-4 after three lost fourth quarter leads, with Nico Collins back
matchup: Houston is a 6.5 to 7.5 point road favorite. ESPN's feed has 6.5 after opening the week at 7, nflverse has 7.5 with a minus 355 money line, and the total is 38.5; the power ratings have Houston 16th at an Elo of 1502 against Tennessee's 32nd at 1244, and the Texans are 0-4 against the closing spread, per nflverse.

Stroud against the 30th ranked secondary decides it. C.J. Stroud has 1,141 yards, 5 touchdowns and no interceptions on 151 attempts, and Houston gains 20 or more yards on 10.5 percent of throws, 7th; Tennessee allows 0.20 EPA per dropback, 29th, and intercepts or breaks up 10.5 percent of dropbacks, 29th.

A close game works against them. Houston led in the fourth quarter of three of its four losses: 31-30 over Buffalo with 6:44 left, at Indianapolis before a 53 yard field goal won it 19-17, and over Dallas until CeeDee Lamb's touchdown with 40 seconds left; Tennessee's last three losses were by 4, 5 and 6 points.
strengths: Nico Collins is back and producing. 7 catches for 118 yards and 2 touchdowns against Dallas after missing two games with a hamstring; he has 14 catches for 193 yards and 3 touchdowns in his two games, the only two in which Houston has scored 30 or more.

C.J. Stroud has not thrown an interception. 151 attempts without one, and Sunday's 21 of 31 for 347 yards and 2 touchdowns, 11.2 yards an attempt, made him PFF's quarterback of the week, per Athlon and FantasyPros.

The pass rush ranks with the best. 14 sacks, 3.5 a game, tied 3rd, and the front ranks 5th in the tracker with pressure on 27.5 percent of dropbacks, 6th; Will Anderson Jr. (4.5 sacks, per nflverse), Danielle Hunter and Sheldon Rankins (2 each) face a Tennessee line ranked 21st.

The big plays have arrived. 4.8 plays of 20 or more yards a game, tied 3rd; Jaylin Noel has 8 catches for 186 yards, 23.3 a catch, including 3 for 85 on Sunday, and Dalton Schultz leads the team with 21 catches for 214 yards.

The pass defense is better than the points say. It ranks 7th in the site's units and allows minus 0.01 EPA per dropback, 9th, with Derek Stingley Jr., Kamari Lassiter and Jalen Pitre, against a Tennessee offense scoring 13.8 points a game, 31st, behind a quarterback unit ranked 32nd.
weaknesses: The run game is near the bottom. David Montgomery has 127 yards on 47 carries, 2.7 a carry, and the backs managed 46 yards on 16 carries Sunday; the backfield ranks 29th in the tracker at 3.7 yards a carry, 30th, against a Tennessee front ranked 9th.

The defense leaks points late. 27.3 points allowed a game, tied 26th; Dallas scored 28 in the second half Sunday, with Javonte Williams running for 3 touchdowns and CeeDee Lamb catching 17 passes for 189 yards.

The linebackers are thin. Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) missed Week 4 after DeMeco Ryans called him week to week, Kenneth Murray Jr. was evaluated for a concussion against Dallas, and Henry To'oTo'o and Jake Hummel are on injured reserve.

More bodies went down. Corner Jaylin Smith (hamstring) went on injured reserve Tuesday after leaving the Dallas game, defensive tackle Jaden Crumedy hurt a shoulder Sunday, and running back British Brooks (hamstring) went on IR Friday; Mario Edwards Jr. (torn ACL) is already out.

Stroud takes too many sacks. 3.0 sacks allowed a game, tied 25th, behind a line ranked 24th in the tracker with right tackle Braden Smith on injured reserve, though DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Smith's 21 day practice window would open Wednesday along with Tank Dell's and Kayden McDonald's, per AP and the team's site; third downs convert at 35.2 percent, 21st.
keys: Throw early and often. Tennessee's secondary is 30th in the tracker and its front 9th, so lean on C.J. Stroud to Nico Collins and Jaylin Noel rather than a run game averaging 2.7 a carry with David Montgomery.

Get home on Cam Ward. Houston has 3.5 sacks a game, tied 3rd, against a passer at 6.1 yards an attempt; Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter against Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham is where the game turns.

Finish the fourth quarter. Three fourth quarter leads became losses; in the week's lowest total, turn red zone trips into touchdowns, where Houston scores on 57.1 percent, tied 15th, with Ka'imi Fairbairn (7 of 8 on field goals) as the backstop.

TEN.headline: 0-4 and 32nd in the power ratings, coming off Ward's and Tate's best day
matchup: Tennessee is a 6.5 to 7.5 point home underdog. ESPN's feed has 6.5, nflverse 7.5 with the Titans at plus 280 on the money line, and the 38.5 total is the week's lowest; Tennessee covered as an 11.5 point underdog at Baltimore, where Lamar Jackson left with an ankle injury and Tyler Huntley played the second half.

Cam Ward against Houston's rush decides it. The Titans allow 1.5 sacks a game, tied 5th, but Houston gets 3.5, tied 3rd; Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham draw Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter, and Ward ranks 32nd at minus 0.16 EPA per dropback.

The secondary works against them. It ranks 30th in the tracker and allows 0.20 EPA per dropback, 29th, against C.J. Stroud, who threw for 347 yards Sunday, and Nico Collins, who caught 2 touchdowns in his return.
strengths: The defense keeps it close. 20.8 points allowed a game, tied 9th, and 5.2 yards a play, tied 12th; the last three losses came by 4, 5 and 6 points.

Carnell Tate had his first 100 yard game. 9 catches on 12 targets for 145 yards at Baltimore; the No. 4 pick leads the team with 22 catches for 268 yards, and Wan'Dale Robinson has 16 for 123 and 2 touchdowns.

Cam Ward played his best game. 20 of 31 for 222 yards, his season high, with a touchdown, an interception, 27 rushing yards and a 2 point conversion throw; Robert Saleh called it his best game this year and said the team has the utmost confidence in him.

The front matches up with Houston's line. Tennessee's front ranks 9th in the tracker and allows minus 0.06 rush EPA a carry, 13th, with Jeffery Simmons inside; Houston's line ranks 24th and allows 3.0 sacks a game, tied 25th.

The pocket has held up, and the starters are back. 1.5 sacks allowed a game, tied 5th, 6 in four games for Cam Ward, per nflverse; Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears and John Franklin-Myers all played at Baltimore after missing practice the Wednesday before.
weaknesses: The offense cannot score. 13.8 points a game, 31st, never more than 20 in a game, 4.9 yards a play, tied 24th, and touchdowns on 50 percent of red zone trips, tied 23rd.

Cam Ward is 3-18 as a starter. 726 yards, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions this season at 6.1 yards an attempt; last week the Tennessean noted he was the 7th quarterback since 1950 to lose 17 of his first 20 starts.
There is no deep game. 2.8 plays of 20 or more yards a game, tied 22nd, and 7.4 percent of throws gain 20 or more, 29th in the tracker, where the receivers rank 24th.

The secondary ranks 30th. 0.20 EPA allowed per dropback, 29th, and an interception or breakup on 10.5 percent of dropbacks, 29th; Cor'Dale Flott, Alontae Taylor, Amani Hooker and Kevin Winston Jr. face a passer with no interceptions in 151 throws.

Right guard is on its third option. Fernando Carmona (ankle) and Jackson Slater (foot, eligible Week 8) went on injured reserve Sept. 29; Atonio Mafi is listed as the starter as of Wednesday's depth chart, with Garrett Dellinger behind him; the line ranks 21st in the tracker.
keys: Lean on Tony Pollard. He has 221 yards on 54 carries, 4.1 a carry; Houston's run defense ranks 4th in the site's units, but it played Week 4 without Azeez Al-Shaair and has Henry To'oTo'o and Jake Hummel on injured reserve, and long drives keep C.J. Stroud on the sideline.
Get the ball out quickly. Houston sacks 3.5 times a game, tied 3rd; quick throws to Carnell Tate (22 catches) and Wan'Dale Robinson (16) keep Will Anderson Jr. off Cam Ward.
Stay within one score into the fourth. Houston has lost three games it led in the fourth quarter, and Tennessee's last three losses came by 4, 5 and 6 points, so the Titans need it close late.

CIN.headline: Two straight losses, Chase and Higgins in doubt, and a winless Miami next
matchup: Cincinnati is a 7 point road favorite. nflverse has them at minus 355 on the money line, and the 42.5 total on ESPN's feed as of Tuesday puts the Bengals near 25 points and Miami near 18; no expert picks were in when this was written, and the Wednesday report on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins is the swing.

The deciding matchup is Joe Burrow against a secondary without Reese Taylor. Miami's defensive backs rank 31st in the site's units, with passes picked or defensed on 10.3 percent of dropbacks, 30th; Burrow threw for 428 yards in Sunday's 22-17 loss to Jacksonville, per ESPN's box and nflverse, and Cincinnati converts 45.3 percent of third downs, 7th.

Working against them is the run defense. Cincinnati ranks 27th against the run in the site's units, and Ollie Gordon II ran 9 times for 100 yards and a touchdown at Minnesota, per ESPN's box, behind a Miami line averaging 4.5 yards a carry, 7th.

keys: Take the ball from Drake Maye. He has 7 interceptions in four games and lost a fumble at Buffalo; Hezekiah Masses, Nakobe Dean and Jeremy Chinn have to turn pressure into the takeaways that won the first three games and were missing against Kansas City.

Feed Bowers and give Washington his carries. Brock Bowers has 202 yards in two games, while Mike Washington Jr. averages 5.0 a carry to Ashton Jeanty's 3.4, against a New England front 25th in rush EPA allowed.

NE.headline: Favored at home after the Buffalo upset, with Maye's interceptions and Hollins' calf the worries

keys: Give the Raiders nothing to take. Las Vegas forced 9 turnovers in its first three games and Nakobe Dean forced a fumble in each, per the Review-Journal; Drake Maye cannot add to his league high 7 interceptions.

Take Brock Bowers away. 16 catches for 202 yards in two games; Robert Spillane, Craig Woodson and Kevin Byard have to make Kirk Cousins beat them with a receiver room missing Jalen Nailor (concussion), Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. (both injured reserve).

The left side of the line is gone or in doubt. Left guard Donovan Jackson tore his meniscus and faces likely season ending surgery, per O'Connell, and left tackle Christian Darrisaw is in concussion protocol as of Tuesday, per ESPN, the Star Tribune, Yahoo and the Pioneer Press; the line already ranks 32nd in the site's units with a 10.8 percent sack rate allowed, 32nd.

The offense does not finish drives. No touchdown Sunday, a 50 percent red zone touchdown rate, tied for 23rd, and 34.4 percent on third down, 25th; Minnesota's quarterbacks rank 31st in EPA a dropback, minus 0.14, in the site's units.

There are few big plays. 2.8 plays of 20 or more yards a game, tied for 22nd, and 4.4 yards a play, 32nd; with Jefferson out Sunday, Jordan Addison caught 4 for 52 and Jauan Jennings 1 for 8, per ESPN's feed, and on Wednesday the Vikings signed Odell Beckham Jr., released by the Giants, to the practice squad, per KSTP and Yahoo.

keys: Get after Tyler Shough early. Blitz a line without Kelvin Banks Jr. that allows 3.0 sacks a game, tied for 25th; Dallas Turner, with 5.5 sacks, Andrew Van Ginkel and Blake Cashman lead a front getting 4.0 sacks a game, 1st, and a sack fumble started the Saints' Week 3 collapse.

Run Aaron Jones at a defense that just gave up 205 rushing yards. Atlanta ran for 205 and 5 touchdowns Monday, per AP, NBC and Fox; Jones had 20 carries for 94 yards Sunday, and a long day on the ground protects a line missing Donovan Jackson.

Finish red zone trips with touchdowns. Five field goals beat Miami, but New Orleans scores touchdowns on 80 percent of its red zone trips, tied for 4th, to Minnesota's 50 percent, tied for 23rd; T.J. Hockenson, 13 of 13 for 119 yards Sunday, is the target inside the 20.

keys: Get the ball out against Brian Flores' blitz. Stop Aaron Jones and make Kyler Murray throw it. Atlanta's 205 rushing yards cannot repeat; Minnesota averages 4.4 yards a play, 32nd, and its quarterbacks rank 31st in EPA a dropback in the site's units, with Justin Jefferson not cleared as of Tuesday.

Trade touchdowns for field goals in the red zone. CLE.headline: Three close wins, ten days of rest, and no Mason Graham

weaknesses: Mason Graham is expected to miss the game. A grade 2 MCL sprain and a grade 1 ankle sprain from the Pittsburgh game, found on an MRI Friday, Oct 2; NFL.com's Ian Rapoport, Heavy and Yardbarker say he likely misses Weeks 5 and 6, though ESPN's feed still had him questionable Tuesday.
